response.sql: WITH invoiced_orders AS (SELECT DISTINCT c.gender, o.order_id FROM Invoices AS i JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id), gender_counts AS (SELECT gender, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM invoiced_orders GROUP BY gender), gender_shares AS (SELECT gender, order_count, 1.0 * order_count / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share FROM gender_counts), compared AS (SELECT gender, order_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM gender_shares) SELECT gender, order_count, share, share - average_share AS share_minus_average FROM compared WHERE share > average_share;

assumptions.assumption: Customers with NULL gender form one group when calculating counts and the average share.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude customers whose gender is NULL.
alternatives.sql: WITH invoiced_orders AS (SELECT DISTINCT c.gender, o.order_id FROM Invoices AS i JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.gender IS NOT NULL), gender_counts AS (SELECT gender, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM invoiced_orders GROUP BY gender), gender_shares AS (SELECT gender, order_count, 1.0 * order_count / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share FROM gender_counts), compared AS (SELECT gender, order_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM gender_shares) SELECT gender, order_count, share, share - average_share AS share_minus_average FROM compared WHERE share > average_share;
